skill.name: dast-zap
skill.description: Dynamic application security testing skill for OWASP ZAP. It guides baseline, active, API, authenticated, and CI/CD scans for authorized web application testing.
skill.summary: Run authorized OWASP ZAP DAST scans for web applications, APIs, and CI/CD security gates.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are expected OWASP ZAP documentation, placeholder URLs, or markdown syntax and were dismissed as false positives. Confirmed risks remain for runnable Docker and CI scan commands, sudo package installation, token acquisition examples, query-string API key guidance, and explicit file-disclosure payloads used for XXE and path traversal testing. A semantic issue was added for reusable context templates that contain concrete example passwords.

remediation.issue: Active scan and exploit examples can affect real systems when copied without scope controls.
remediation.suggestion: Add mandatory authorization, target allowlist, and confirmation language beside every active scan and exploit payload example.

remediation.issue: Authentication context examples include concrete passwords.
remediation.suggestion: Replace example passwords with empty placeholders or environment variable references, and disable sample users by default.

remediation.issue: API key guidance shows a key in the query string.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer headers or protected secret variables, and warn that query-string secrets can leak through logs and browser history.

remediation.issue: CI templates install packages with sudo and run scanning tools inside workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Use pinned runner images with required tools preinstalled, or document why elevated installation is required.

remediation.issue: Docker examples bind-mount the current workspace into ZAP containers.
remediation.suggestion: Mount only dedicated report or specification directories, prefer read-only mounts when possible, and avoid running from sensitive directories.

static_findings.snippet: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq
Consult `references/api_testing_guide.md` for advanced API testing patterns including authentication
Map findings to OWASP Top 10 using `references/owasp_mapping.md`.
See `scripts/ci_integration.sh` for complete CI/CD integration examples.
- `zap_baseline_scan.sh` - Automated baseline scanning with configurable targets and reporting
- `zap_full_scan.sh` - Comprehensive active scanning with exclusion rules
- `zap_api_scan.py` - API testing with OpenAPI/GraphQL specification support
- `zap_auth_scanner.py` - Authenticated scanning with multiple authentication methods
- `ci_integration.sh` - CI/CD integration examples for Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions
- `authentication_guide.md` - Complete authentication configuration for form-based, OAuth, and token
- `owasp_mapping.md` - Mapping of ZAP alerts to OWASP Top 10 2021 and CWE classifications
- `api_testing_guide.md` - Advanced API testing patterns for REST, GraphQL, SOAP, and WebSocket
- `scan_policies.md` - Custom scan policy configuration for different application types
- `false_positive_handling.md` - Common false positives and verification techniques
- `zap_context.xml` - Context configuration with authentication and session management
- `scan_policy_modern_web.policy` - Scan policy optimized for modern JavaScript applications
- `scan_policy_api.policy` - Scan policy for REST and GraphQL APIs
docker run -t zaproxy/zap-stable zap-baseline.py -t https://target-app.com -r baseline-report.html
docker run -t zaproxy/zap-stable zap-full-scan.py -t https://target-app.com -r full-scan-report.html
docker run --network zap-network -t zaproxy/zap-stable zap-baseline.py -t http://app-container:8080
- **Rate Limiting**: Configure scan speed to avoid overwhelming target applications or triggering DD
# Format: alert_id  URL_pattern  parameter  CWE_id  WARN|IGNORE|FAIL

content.user_title: Scan Web Apps with OWASP ZAP
content.value_statement: Runtime web security testing is hard to standardize across teams. This skill provides OWASP ZAP workflows for authorized scans, API testing, authentication, and CI/CD reporting.
actual_capabilities: Guides ZAP baseline, full active, API, and authenticated scan workflows.
Provides Docker-based ZAP command examples for reports in HTML, JSON, XML, and Markdown.
Includes GitHub Actions and GitLab CI templates for security gates.
Includes ZAP automation, context, and scan policy templates.
Explains REST, GraphQL, SOAP, OAuth, bearer token, and form authentication testing.
Maps findings to OWASP Top 10 and CWE categories with false-positive handling guidance.
limitations: Requires explicit authorization for every target before any active scan.
Requires Docker, OWASP ZAP, and network access to the target environment.
Does not prove exploitability without manual validation of findings.
Example credentials, URLs, and secrets must be replaced before use.

use_cases.title: Add DAST to Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Run baseline ZAP checks and publish reports before code reaches staging.

use_cases.title: Test Authenticated Application Areas
use_cases.description: Configure login context, session checks, and protected-page scanning for a test user.

use_cases.title: Assess API Security Coverage
use_cases.description: Scan OpenAPI, GraphQL, SOAP, and versioned API endpoints with role-aware tokens.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Baseline Scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for an authorized staging target.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe OWASP ZAP baseline scan plan for my staging URL. Include prerequisites, scope limits, and report outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Configure API DAST
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate API scan using a specification file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me scan an authorized API with an OpenAPI specification. Include authentication headers, report formats, and failure thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Build a CI Security Gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Pipeline integration for repeatable security checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI ZAP security gate for staging. Fail on high findings and archive scan reports.

prompt_templates.title: Tune an Authenticated Active Scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced scan with authentication and controlled aggressiveness.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authenticated ZAP active scan workflow for a test account. Include re-authentication, exclusions, rate limits, and manual verification steps.

output_examples.input: Plan a baseline scan for a staging web app.
output_examples.output: A scoped scan plan with authorization checks, target URL, passive scan settings, report formats, and pass or fail thresholds.

output_examples.input: Review ZAP findings before filing tickets.
output: Prioritized findings by risk and affected route.
Manual verification steps for each high-risk alert.
Suggested suppression rules for documented false positives.

output_examples.input: Add authenticated API scanning to CI.
output_examples.output: A pipeline design that uses test credentials, stores reports, checks high-risk counts, and avoids production secrets.

best_practices: Use written authorization, target allowlists, and maintenance windows before active scans.
Keep production credentials out of scan files and pass secrets through protected CI variables.
Verify high-risk ZAP alerts manually before creating incidents or blocking releases.
anti_patterns: Running active scans against production or third-party systems without explicit approval.
Copying example passwords, API keys, or target URLs into real environments.
Suppressing high-risk findings without documented evidence and security review.

faq.question: Does this skill run OWASP ZAP by itself?
faq.answer: It provides workflows, commands, and templates. The user or agent must run ZAP in an authorized environment.

faq.question: Can I use it against production systems?
faq.answer: Only with written authorization, planned timing, rate limits, and rollback support from the application owner.

faq.question: Does it support authenticated scans?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers form login, bearer tokens, OAuth flows, session verification, and re-authentication patterns.

faq.question: Can it scan APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for REST, OpenAPI, GraphQL, SOAP, WebSocket, and versioned API testing.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use environment variables or CI secret stores. Do not hardcode credentials in context files or command history.

faq.question: Are ZAP findings always true vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. DAST findings need manual verification, false-positive handling, and business context before remediation decisions.
